grammar.title: 2B: Present perfect + for / since, present perfect continuous
grammar.explanation:
Use the **present perfect** for things that started in the past and are still true now. **I have played** football for two years, and I still **play**.

Use **for** with a **period of time**: for two years, for one hour. **She has run** every morning for one year.

Use **since** with a **point in time**: since Monday, since January. Our **team** has **won** games since January.

Use **have / has been + verb-ing** for actions that started in the past and are still happening now. **I have been swimming** for one hour.

Our **coach** has been teaching us to **score** **goals** since last year. We still **jump** and kick the **ball** with him.
examples: I have *played* football *for* two years. (for = a period of time)
She has *run* every morning *since* January. (since = a point in time)
Our *team* has *won* games *for* a long time.
I have been *swimming* *for* one hour. (I am still in the pool now)
He has been *jumping* *since* this morning. (he is still jumping now)
Our *coach* has been *teaching* us *since* last year. (he still teaches us)

practice.q: Which is correct: 'I have played for Monday' or 'I have played since Monday'?
practice.a: 'I have played since Monday' — use **since** with a point in time like Monday.

practice.q: Complete the sentence: She has been ___ (swim) for one hour.
practice.a: She has been **swimming** for one hour.

practice.q: 'How long have you played football?' — what does this question ask?
practice.a: It asks about an unfinished period of time, from the past until now.
